faqs.q: How do I create a Seedance 2.5 Flash video?
faqs.a: Select Flash in the workspace, choose Create, Modify or Extend and supply the inputs requested by that mode. Review the current quote before confirming.
Up to 10 images, 5 videos and 5 audio clips, within the selected mode’s limits. Audio references require a visual input. Edit and extension use their own source-video controls.

faqs.q: Does Flash include 1080p, 4K or native Draft/final?
faqs.a: No. Flash outputs 480p or 720p. Standard Seedance 2.5 has its own 1080p and native Draft-to-final workflow. A Flash generation cannot be finalized as a native Draft.

faqs.q: Are these prompts real Flash results?
faqs.a: The Prompt Lab contains editable scene plans. A video example is attributed to Flash only when it was actually generated by that model.

faqs.q: Where can I see the price?
faqs.a: The page shows current quotes for its sample settings. Your final quote is calculated in the workspace from the model, duration, resolution, audio and source inputs.

section.title: Prompt Lab — direct a Flash scene
section.intro: Adapt these scene-planning prompts to your subject, action and camera. A prompt template describes an intended result; it is not a completed generation.
section.tip: Change one visible choice between variants so you can compare the results.

tabs.label: Character
tabs.title: Give the scene a clear subject
tabs.description: Describe the character and the moment you want to see.
tabs.copy: A courier in a red jacket pauses under the awning of a rain-soaked city street at night. She notices a familiar silhouette across the road, turns toward it and smiles. Keep her jacket, face and the wet street lighting consistent.

tabs.label: Action
tabs.title: Make the movement readable
tabs.description: Set an opening, one action and a final composition.
tabs.copy: Begin with a medium view of a dancer waiting beside a sunlit studio window. She takes one step, turns smoothly and settles facing the window. Keep her hands and feet visible during the turn. Finish with a still composition.

tabs.label: Camera
tabs.title: Try one camera variation
tabs.description: Keep the subject and action fixed while changing the framing.
tabs.copy: Keep the same courier, location and action. Version A: a slow lateral tracking shot at eye level. Version B: a gentle push from a medium view to a close-up as she smiles. Avoid extra cuts.

globalPrinciples: Describe the action in the order it happens.
Use a camera movement that can follow the subject.
Repeat only the visual details that must stay stable.

cinematic.intro: Five scenes, five different creative briefs. Explore the camera movement, human action and sound direction that can turn a first frame into a film.

assetTitles.title: Midnight run — a low tracking shot
After the beat — a live performance
The blue hour — a quiet exchange

cinematic.provenance: These six stills, including the hero, were generated with GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst. They are animation start frames, not Seedance 2.5 Flash videos or proof of its motion, audio, speed or consistency. Real renders will replace the illustrations after review.

panels.title: Something happens. We feel it.
panels.body: A drumstick held before the strike. A look before a reply. Start with a readable human action and a camera move that gives it space.
panels.note: These are planned scenes. Timing, lip sync, hand motion and generated sound still need to be evaluated in the actual video.

panels.title: Make the impossible feel physical.
panels.body: An astronaut, an abandoned opera house and a creature suspended overhead. Define what moves, what stays still and how the camera discovers the scene.
panels.note: This first frame sets the visual direction. It does not establish how Flash will handle gravity, continuity or interaction.

panels.title: Small screen. Full presence.
panels.body: A coat catches the light. A skateboarder commits to the drop. Compose for 9:16 from the start, with a clear subject and room for movement.
panels.note: The source images are portrait start frames. Output framing, motion and audio will be checked in the future renders.

shotPlans.motion: A short drum fill. The camera arcs around the kit and finishes on her expression.
shotPlans.sound: Close snare and tom hits, cymbal decay and distant rooftop ambience.

shotPlans.motion: A gentle push toward the two actors, a short exchange, then a held silence.
shotPlans.sound: Two separate voices, quiet room tone and rain against the window.

shotPlans.motion: Follow the astronaut’s gaze as the creature glides through the opera house; hold the architecture steady.
shotPlans.sound: Footsteps, a spacious room echo and a low, restrained atmospheric sound.

shotPlans.motion: Track the walk through the colonnade; let the coat move naturally as she crosses the light.
shotPlans.sound: Footsteps and fabric movement in an airy stone corridor.

shotPlans.motion: A controlled drop and a short follow-through, keeping the board and body readable.
shotPlans.sound: Wheels on concrete, the landing impact and a brief open-air ambience.
